text.title: Refusal Field Strict Schema Core Rules
text.summary: 6 testable rules every refusal-field-strict-schema spec MUST enforce. Declare nullable refusal first so safety declines parse cleanly into a typed branch instead of breaking strict-mode JSON.

section.title: Background
section.p: OpenAI's strict-mode response already includes a top-level `refusal` string when the model declines. Mirroring it inside your own schema gives the same contract on Anthropic and local backends and turns refusal handling from exception-driven into typed-branch code.

rule.statement: The output schema MUST include a top-level optional string `refusal` field.
rule.rationale: Top-level makes branching cheap; nested means every consumer has to drill in.

rule.statement: When using OpenAI Responses API, `strict: true` MUST be set on the schema.
rule.rationale: Non-strict mode lets the model wander outside the schema.

rule.statement: Caller code MUST check `output.refusal` before processing other fields; on non-null, return early.
rule.rationale: Without branching, the agent acts on stub/empty fields and corrupts state.

rule.statement: Refusal text MUST be logged for safety review.
rule.rationale: Refusal patterns inform prompt or policy adjustments.

rule.statement: Prompts MUST NOT instruct the model to refuse; the model picks based on policy, the schema accommodates.

For any strict-mode SO schema in a safety-sensitive domain, add `refusal: str | None = None` as the FIRST field; mark every payload field nullable; check `response.refusal` in a single branch before reading the payload.
rule.rationale: Strict mode forbids missing required fields; without a refusal channel the model must either invent fake values or violate the grammar. The explicit field gives the model a legal path to decline.
